newsitem.title: UK: England cricketer Botham to appeal in libel case.
newsitem.headline: England cricketer Botham to appeal in libel case.

text.p: A lawyer for Ian Botham said on Monday the former England cricketer would seek a retrial after losing an expensive libel battle against Imran Khan in July.
Botham and fellow England star Allan Lamb accused the former Pakistan captain of calling them uneducated racists, but after 13 days the High Court rejected their case.
Lawyer Rhory Robertson said Botham would appeal on the grounds that the judge had misdirected the jury during the action, which left the two men facing legal bills of up to 500,000 pounds ($750,000).

"That will go to the Court of Appeal. The case is likely to be heard in the summer of next year," he told reporters, adding that Lamb was still considering his position and would make a decision after meeting his legal team on Wednesday.

Both players took Imran to court over what they described as an "offensive personal attack" on them in India Today magazine which they said called them racist, uneducated and lacking class and upbringing.

Much of the hearing centred on ball-tampering -- the illicit practice of altering the state of the ball during a match. Huge crowds in the public gallery watched a parade of English cricketing legends give evidence.
